items.text: SEASON 8 · EPISODE 10 · DRAFT · SEASON FINALE  Opening day · Maya, Kit, Nkechi, Bram, Tove, Dario, Odile and Marshal Lindqvist · Level L5 · Advanced support (formulas on request)  The Wyndmere Centre opens tonight, sold out. The building is weeks from finished, and nobody comes in until the marshal signs.  ⚑ RV-160 / RV-162 / RV-163: every system on the map belongs to someone; nobody goes at height; nothing in a life-safety interface is ever jumpered. MD-01 / MD-02: the season boss. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Opening Night, Unfinished
items.stakes: The Wyndmere opens tonight, sold out, weeks from finished. Nobody comes in until the marshal signs.
items.clock: Ninety minutes to the marshal's deadline.
items.reward: A building that opens safe — proven where the people sit — with every gap written down.

objectives.text: Decide what happens when the fiber goes

items.rumor: Everything this season taught, in ninety minutes.

items.alt: The finished main hall, empty seats, a clock chip reading 16:30; Odile points at the seats; Maya beside her with a clipboard.

bubbles.text: Sold out. Marshal at six. Tell me what can go wrong.
Everything. So we do it in order.

items.caption: Nobody comes in until the marshal signs.

lines.text: Sold out. The marshal at six. Tell me what can go wrong.
Everything. So we do it in order.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #81 · AVERY'S LENS  Open with the gaps written down  An unfinished building can open safely if every known gap is written down, owned and dated — and life safety is proven, not assumed.  The Wyndmere opened with a foyer on a still slide, a broadcast room closed and temporary power — and every one of them on a list with a name.
Act I — “The pair the drawings promised”

items.alt: The east wall near the dock: a parked lift, a dangling fiber cable with a torn end; Kit on the floor well clear of the lift, pointing at the cut.

bubbles.text: The lift caught the north riser. The core's on one cut pair.

items.prompt: 16:40. The north riser fiber is cut. The core runs on it. What now?
items.risk: A dark house on opening night.

hints.text: What did the drawings promise in week one?

options.label: Ask the lift operator to take Kit back up to look at the cut
options.result: Bram: “Nobody goes up to look at anything today.”
options.consequence: A person at height for a look.
options.fail: Nobody goes up for a look.

options.label: Ask the network contractor to bring the core up on the spare south pair — you know its loss: 1.92 dB of a 6.2 dB budget, 4.28 dB of margin
options.result: The south pair lights in four minutes. The core never goes fully dark.
options.consequence: The path the design promised in week one.

options.label: Run a temporary network cable across the hall from the MER
options.result: Three hundred metres. Copper Ethernet stops at a hundred.

options.label: Wait for a fusion splicer tomorrow
options.result: The house has no stage audio tonight.

items.title: The retest rule caught it.
items.body: 16:55. Nkechi runs her pre-test — the rule from punch 188: any change to a rack with a life-safety interface means a retest before doors. Stage right fails: program plays through the alarm, and the panel shows TROUBLE on the stage-right relay circuit. Punch 402, closed at 15:20 — ‘replace amp rack fan’ — knocked a wire loose in the fire alarm contractor's relay module. Found at five to five, not in front of the marshal at six.
items.label: Test: how many minutes — and whose repair?

items.sub: Advanced · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Maya and Kit beside a board. Tonight is every number from this season at once: the fiber budget, the preheat current, the mute time. South pair: one point nine two dB lost, four point two eight of margin. Preheat in three groups of fourteen point four amps. Mute in point six five seconds. And none of them counts until the marshal has watched it work.

items.caption: Advanced: the formula is there if you ask. Try without it first.

items.text: 📙 ON REQUEST · ADVANCED  Terms   Certificate of occupancy   Authority having jurisdiction   Fire watch   Temporary power   If you need it   ƒ Ask for the formula · Optical loss budget   ƒ FORMULA · Optical loss budget  L = α × d + n c  × L c  + n s  × L s  · margin = budget − L   α  fiber attenuation, dB/km  d  length, km  n c , L c   mated connector pairs and the loss allowed for each, dB  n s , L s   splices and the loss allowed for each, dB  budget  the transceiver's allowed channel loss, dB      ƒ Ask for the formula · Current from power   ƒ FORMULA · Current from power  I = P ÷ V   I  current, A  P  power, W  V  voltage, V

items.label: **Learn it now:** opening under conditions — everything at once, in order.

items.text: 📖 From the Fieldbook · tap a plate to open it full size     Point it at people, not at the ceiling     Sound that brings people in     What the room is telling you

items.prompt: 16:57. Bram: “The marshal's coming and the panel says trouble. Just jumper the circuit so it reads normal. We'll fix it properly tomorrow.”
items.risk: A building that can't open — or one that opens unsafe.
timeout: Bram sends his electrician to ‘have a look’.
The fire alarm contractor stops him at the rack — twenty minutes lost.

hints.text: Whose circuit is it — and what would you show the marshal?

options.label: Jumper it — just for tonight
options.result: A life-safety system that lies to the marshal and to the audience.
options.consequence: Removes the safety to pass the test.
options.fail: Nothing in a life-safety interface is ever jumpered.

options.label: No. It's the fire alarm contractor's circuit: their tech repairs it; then a retest with the fire alarm contractor at the panel and Nkechi timing. And ask Bram to keep every trade out of the racks until doors
options.result: Their tech re-terminates the wire by 17:12. The retest: 0.7 s on stage right. Bram puts a man on the rack-room door.
options.consequence: Say no, say why, give him a job.

options.label: Ask the marshal to test only stage left
Put the panel in test mode until the show's over
options.result: A fire alarm system switched off, with 1,400 people inside.
options.fail: Nothing in a life-safety system is disabled.

items.title: “Absolutely fireproof”
items.body: In November 1903 Chicago's Iroquois Theatre opened, advertised as ‘absolutely fireproof’, with work unfinished and fire equipment missing. Five weeks later, at a packed holiday matinee, a stage light set a curtain alight. The safety curtain jammed, many exits were locked or hidden behind drapes, and more than 600 people died. Cities rewrote their theatre codes: outward-opening exits, push bars, marked exits. A building is ready when its safety is proven — not when it's advertised.

items.alt: The MER at 17:05: the racks steady; a clock chip; Kit and Maya listening to a radio call from Tove.

bubbles.text: Preheat group one — up. Group two in two minutes. Group three at nine past. My board held.

narration: At 16:35 Maya had given Tove one number: 16 × 108 W ÷ 120 V = 14.4 A a group. Tove chose the sequence.
items.caption: Her panel. Her sequence.

items.title: ‘replace amp rack fan’ · 15:20
items.body: Punch 402, closed at 15:20 today: ‘Stage-right amp rack — replace failed fan.’ Under it, in Nkechi's hand: ‘Rack holds life-safety interface — RETEST before doors.’ The rule from punch 188, doing its job.

items.title: The marshal is early.
items.body: 17:30. Marshal Lindqvist walks in half an hour early: “I'll test at quarter to six. Every station. And I'll listen from the house.” Meanwhile the truck at the dock needs a program feed — the core has the room: 620 plus 150 on a 1,000 Mb/s uplink is 77% — and sixty foyer decoders on 3.9 have been fenced onto the staging VLAN with a still slide.
items.label: Test: the mute time — and how long you have.

items.alt: The main hall at 17:45; the fire alarm panel in ALARM; Marshal Lindqvist listening from the aisle; Nkechi with a stopwatch. No music notes in the air.

bubbles.text: My message. Nothing under it. Three stations, three times.
Zero point seven, zero point six, zero point seven.

items.caption: She signs the temporary certificate of occupancy.

items.prompt: You said no to me in front of my crew.

options.label: “I did. And I'd rather you heard it from me at five than from the marshal at six. You put someone on the rack-room door — that's why stage right held.”
“You'd have got us all shut down.”
options.reply: Maybe. You could've said it quieter.

items.alt: Maya in the half-finished hall in amber work light, radio in hand. Around her, stamped over the scene: fiber cut, trouble, TP-2?, marshal.
narration: Everything above happened one call at a time. On opening day it didn't. From 16:30 to 18:00 every fault touched every other one.
items.caption: Take Maya's radio. Open the building.

items.label: **☢ Meltdown:** ninety minutes, all at once — contain, reroute, hand power to its owner, prove. Half the map isn't yours.

items.prompt: 18:10. Odile: “We're signed. Doors at half past. What do we open with?”
unknown: What the venue team will find
items.risk: A handover built on things nobody wrote down.
timeout: The venue team learns about TP-2 when it trips.

hints.text: What does the person running this building tomorrow need in their hand?

options.label: Keep quiet about what isn't finished — it's opening night
options.result: The venue's technicians find the foyer, the broadcast room and TP-2 one surprise at a time.

options.label: Open — with every known gap written down, owned and dated: foyer screens on a still slide (Dario, Tuesday, on staging), broadcast room closed (spring), TP-2 until the permanent service is inspected (Tove), the marshal's fire watch on top
options.result: Odile signs the list and hands it to the venue's head technician before doors.
options.consequence: Proven where it matters; owned everywhere else.

options.label: Delay opening a week to finish everything
options.result: 1,400 tickets refunded for a still slide in the foyer.
options.consequence: Costs far more than the gaps.

options.label: Tell the board it's all finished
options.result: The broadcast room is locked with a sign on it.

items.label: **Service Mode:** run the morning after yourself.

items.alt: The main hall at 7:30 p.m.: the house full, the stage lit, the curtain rising; Odile and Maya stand at the back corners of the room.

items.title: Temporary certificate · conditions 1–3
items.body: Marshal Lindqvist's temporary certificate of occupancy: ‘1. Fire watch until the permanent electrical service is inspected. 2. Life-safety interfaces retested after any change. 3. Review in 30 days.’

items.alt: The site trailer after handover week: the punch list roll now short, the gap list pinned on the wall with names beside every line; Kit, Nkechi and Maya.

bubbles.text: Sixteen gaps. Sixteen names. Sixteen dates.
And a building its own people can read.

items.alt: Months later, the lobby during a gala: every display on the wall reads EVACUATE in red; the fire alarm panel beside it reads NORMAL; Kit points; Maya stares.

bubbles.text: The screens say evacuate. The panel says normal.
Then something else is talking to our screens.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  When everything breaks at once: first what gates everything (life safety — repaired by its owner, retested, accepted by the marshal); contain what the night doesn’t need; use the paths the design promised (L = α·d + n·L); hand power to its owner with numbers (I = P ÷ V); check the links before you add to them. Prove it where people sit. Open with every gap written, owned and dated.
REFLECTION (optional)  · If you left tomorrow, what list would the next person need — and does it exist?
